rounds.text: Rajvi Logitrade Ltd trades at a P/E of 16.1x, which sits below its sector benchmark of 18.13x [E1, E6]. This modest multiple contrasts sharply with extraordinary fundamental performance, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 129% and a 3-year compounded profit growth of 152% [E19, E20]. Return metrics are exceptionally strong, featuring a ROCE of 30.09% and an ROE of 27.59% that vastly outperform sector benchmarks of 6.7% and 5.13% respectively [E9, E10]. Operational quality is further confirmed by robust cash conversion of 2.67x against reported profit, generating Rs 8 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 6 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E28, E29, E30]. Confidence in the underlying business is underscored by smart-money accumulation, as foreign institutions have increased their holdings from 0.00% to 25.66% and promoters have raised their stake by nearly 5 percentage points [E34, E35]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% and borrowings carry a high cost [E4, E48].

Despite recent growth figures, Rajvi Logitrade Ltd carries fundamental risks regarding shareholder returns and cost burdens. The dividend yield sits at 0.00% [E4], meaning investors receive zero cash return despite the company reporting repeated profits [E47]. Furthermore, the company's cost of borrowing is flagged as high [E48], which creates an underlying vulnerability even as borrowings decrease to Rs 7 Cr [E32]. Operating margins also show operational inconsistency, reading as inconsistent over the last year annually and over the last three quarters [E26, E27]. Additionally, the stock sits at 100% of the way up its 52-week range [E5], and the price-to-book ratio of 4.46x significantly outpaces the sector benchmark of 1.38x [E2, E7], pointing to an expensive valuation. Conceded: the company displays strong trailing sales growth of 42% alongside robust return metrics such as an ROE of 39.0% and ROCE of 32.4% [E12, E13, E16].

Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4, E47]. However, the absence of dividends is a sign of capital retention fueling massive business expansion, evidenced by a 10-year sales growth of 150% and a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 129% [E14, E20]. While the bear flags high borrowing costs [E48], total borrowings actually decreased from Rs 9 Cr to Rs 7 Cr [E32], and the company generated robust free cash flow of Rs 6 Cr alongside outstanding cash conversion of 2.67x, fully backing profits with cash [E28, E30]. Although operating margins show short-term inconsistency [E26, E27], the broader profitability trend remains exceptional, with an ROE of 39.0% and ROCE of 32.4% that dwarf sector benchmarks [E12, E13, E10, E58]. Finally, the high price-to-book ratio [E2, E7] is entirely justified by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 193 leaving a 57.0% margin of safety, with the current price only requiring a modest 6.4% earnings growth against an 18.0% base case [E37, E38, E39].

Conceded: total borrowings decreased from Rs 9 Cr to Rs 7 Cr [E32]. However, the bull's dismissal of the 0.00% dividend yield ignores the explicit negative flag that the company is reporting repeated profits yet paying out zero dividends [E4, E47]. While the bull highlights strong cash conversion and free cash flow [E28, E30], the evidence directly notes as a negative that the company's cost of borrowing seems high [E48]. Furthermore, the claim that profitability excuses short-term margin volatility overlooks the official record showing that both yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends read inconsistent [E26, E27]. Conceded: the current price implies a 6.4% earnings growth rate [E39]. Finally, relying on a model's intrinsic value and margin of safety [E37, E38] ignores that the rules-based screen explicitly rates confidence as low at 75 out of 100 [E49].
